name: dial
title: Dial
description: A value set by turning a thumb around a circle.
use: A value that is a turn: an angle, a direction, or a level set like a knob, where the circle says more than a line would and the dial has room of its own. It is a role="slider" the behavior moves; a hidden input inside it carries the value to a form.

instead.when: A value along a line, which works without a script and in every form
The value is read, not set
The exact number matters and the reader steps it
The exact number matters and the reader types it

keyboard.action: Turn the value up by a step, clockwise in every writing direction; around a full circle, past the greatest value it comes round to the least
Turn the value down by a step, anticlockwise; around a full circle, below the least it comes round to the greatest
Turn the value up or down by a larger step, a tenth of the range unless the page sets another
Move to aria-valuemin or aria-valuemax; around a full circle, End is the last step before the value comes round

platform.feature: Typed attr(), as in attr(aria-valuenow type(<number>))
platform.fallback: The dial does not read aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax: the behavior writes --dial-value with every change, and the first markup writes it in a style attribute, with --dial-min and --dial-max when the range is not 0 to 100

classes.name: dial
classes.description: The dial, 120px across, on a focusable role="slider" with an accessible name, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax: a round track filled with ink from its start to the value. By default a knob of 270 degrees, open at the foot

classes.name: dial-full
classes.description: The whole circle, starting at the top: an angle, which comes round again past its greatest value

classes.name: dial-thumb
classes.description: The pearl thumb on the track at the value's angle, an empty element. Focus rings it, and a press on it turns the dial without a jump

classes.name: dial-value
classes.description: The value as text, in tabular figures at the middle of the dial; the behavior writes it with every change

classes.name: dial-ticks
classes.description: An empty element that draws --dial-ticks equal steps as fine lines just outside the thumb's path

classes.name: dial-mark
classes.description: A short word or figure in the rim, at the value its --dial-at stands for

states.name: value
states.description: The value, between aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax or 0 and 100. The fill follows it at once

states.name: focus
states.description: The thumb takes the focus ring

states.name: held
states.description: The thumb grows a little while the dial is held, except with reduced motion

states.name: disabled
states.description: The dial fades and takes no pointer, key or wheel

properties.name: --dial-value
properties.description: The value. It comes from aria-valuenow where typed attr() is supported; the behavior writes it too

properties.name: --dial-min
properties.description: The least value. It comes from aria-valuemin where typed attr() is supported

properties.name: --dial-max
properties.description: The greatest value. It comes from aria-valuemax where typed attr() is supported

properties.name: --dial-start
properties.description: Where the least value stands, clockwise from the top; 0deg on dial-full. The behavior reads it to turn a pointer into a value

properties.name: --dial-sweep
properties.description: How far the track runs from the start, clockwise; 360deg on dial-full, which makes the value come round. The behavior reads it too

properties.name: --dial-thumb
properties.description: Thumb diameter; the whole dial takes the pointer

properties.name: --dial-color
properties.description: The ink of the fill; the track is the same color stepped back

properties.name: --dial-ticks
properties.description: How many equal steps the ticks mark across the sweep

properties.name: --dial-at
properties.description: The value a mark stands at

example: 40
